summary:
SYRA is a health and habitat monitoring system that helps astronauts understand onboard conditions and respond without waiting for a reply from Earth. On Mars missions, messages take between 3 and 22 minutes to arrive, requiring the crew to make autonomous decisions.
We have developed a functional system that collects simulated habitat sensor data across ten spacecraft zones and compares it against 25 pre-established rules. Each rule cites its source, such as the NASA-STD-3001 standard or a clearly identified reference value. For every alert, the system provides the measured value, probable cause, and recommended action. Furthermore, our AI agent, SYRA, issues early warnings if a parameter like carbon dioxide rises too rapidly, even before a limit is exceeded.
Crew members can also ask SYRA questions via voice or text, such as "Why do I have a headache?", and receive answers based exclusively on NASA sources, including citations and active environmental alerts. The system also integrates daily health tasks, incident logs, and mission plans sent from mission control.
details:
SYRA was developed as a modular monolith with a hexagonal architecture. The application is organized into well-defined modules, and the core logic is separated from the external tools it depends on, such as databases, frameworks, and communication protocols. Each external tool is connected through an adapter, so it can be replaced quickly and with little impact on the rest of the system. This design avoids dependence on any single tool.

The technologies used in its development are:

Python with FastAPI: Python is the main programming language, and FastAPI is the web framework that handles the backend. FastAPI exposes the application’s endpoints and processes incoming requests and their validation.

PostgreSQL: the relational database that stores the application’s structured data.

pgVector: an extension for PostgreSQL that stores vector embeddings. It is used for the data behind the RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system, which finds the information most relevant to a query by similarity.

GraphQL: a query language for APIs that lets the client request exactly the data it needs in a single request.

REST: an architectural style for APIs based on HTTP resources and standard methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE). It is used for conventional endpoints.

WebSockets: a protocol that keeps a persistent, two-way connection between client and server, so data can be sent in real time without repeated requests.
